title: Octopus-Rex_Botnet_Investigation_26e
description: Investigate and respond to the Octopus-Rex botnet activity, focusing on identifying suspicious services, persistence mechanisms, and abnormal network traffic.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these issues.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim machine with the following credentials:
- Host: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external server?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is likely named 'bot-beacon'.

hints.title: Check running services for unusual network connections
hints.content: Check running services and look for unusual network connections.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Investigate systemd timers and services. The persistence mechanism is likely named 'system-update-checker.timer'.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating the abnormal network traffic?
levels.solution: Analyze network connections and look for services making multiple connections to the same destination. The service is likely named 'bot-flood'.

hints.title: Analyze network connections for abnormal traffic
hints.content: Analyze network connections and look for services making multiple connections to the same destination.
